title: UX Triage Playlist — Q4 2026
body:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic triage for Console & Rollouts UX items to form a Q4 sprint slice. This is intentionally opinionated: create a "playlist" of items that can be run straight through by a design + 2 devs pairing, plus a small set of lower-priority items to hold as fallback.

How this playlist works (ops):
- We score candidate tickets on Customer Impact (0-5), Dev Effort (S/M/L/XL mapped to 1/3/5/8), and Observation/Risk (0-3).
- Compute a simple priority = Impact * 2 - Effort - Risk. Higher is better.
- Playlist is ordered by priority but grouped into three runs: Run A (must do, 1 sprint), Run B (nice-to-have, next sprint), Run C (cut if over capacity).
- Hard cut rule: if Run A dev-total > 13 points, drop lowest-impact medium-effort items first.

Scoring rubric (quick reference):
- Customer Impact: 5 = blocking major customer flows (dedicated/Dedicated onboarding), 3 = common friction for new projects, 1 = edge cosmetic.
- Effort mapping: S=1, M=3, L=5, XL=8. Include QA + observability time in Effort.
- Observability/Risk: 0 = trivial safe change, 1 = needs minor backend support, 2 = affects routing/fallback, 3 = rollout/infra gating (require SRE).

Current candidate set (short-list with quick notes):
1) CON-842 — Route status microcard: show per-route latency/cost microcard on route list (Impact 4, Effort M, Risk 1)
   - Why: product teams repeatedly ask for a quick glance to compare routes without opening route details.
   - UX notes: microcard should include 3 items: 95p latency, avg tokens/token-cost, active model variant. Compact wireframe attached in Confluence.
   - Acceptance: microcard present in list view, accessible via keyboard, metrics refresh on poll.

2) CON-871 — Canary toggle flow simplification (Impact 5, Effort L, Risk 2)
   - Why: canary creation is several-clicks; customers misconfigure fallback policies.
   - UX notes: single-screen canary creation: select baseline model, select canary model, set percent slider, validate fallback policy with inline explanation. Wireframe: right-hand flyout with live preview.
   - Acceptance: create canary in <3 clicks; validation prevented if incompatible model variants.

3) CON-903 — Model routing dropdown: consolidate model variant names, show compatibility badges (Impact 3, Effort S, Risk 1)
   - Short fix: collapse long model ids, add badge if quantized/half-precision.

4) CON-912 — Token cost estimator modal on request preview (Impact 4, Effort M, Risk 1)
   - Add a lightweight estimator that uses last-100-request stats to show median token cost.

5) CON-934 — Rollout activity timeline (Impact 2, Effort L, Risk 2)
   - Visual timeline for canary rollout history (events, traffic changes).

6) CON-955 — Route list filter persistence (Impact 3, Effort S, Risk 0)
   - Keep filters across sessions; add "save view" quick link.

Preliminary playlist assignment (Run A / Run B / Run C):
- Run A (target sprint slice, team capacity ~13 points): CON-842 (M=3), CON-871 (L=5), CON-903 (S=1), CON-955 (S=1) => total 10 points.
- Run B (next sprint): CON-912 (M=3), CON-934 (L=5) => total 8 points.
- Run C (cut/future): any features > L with Impact <=2, plus design debt items.

Wireframe highlights & interaction notes (design quickies):
- Microcard (CON-842): hover reveals two-line expanded metric with a small sparkline; click navigates to route detail. Keyboard: focus state announces model variant + latency.
- Canary single-screen (CON-871): percent slider snaps at 1%, 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%; show predicted latency delta and cost delta live. If fallback is incompatible show inline "Fix fallback" suggestion linking to policy editor.
- Token estimator (CON-912): compute heuristic locally from cached stats to avoid backend call on modal open; fallback to server if stale > 10m.

Open questions / risks (needs decisions this week):
- CON-871 risk 2: do we require SRE to approve canary rollouts that touch routing? If yes, add gate ticket and increase effort.
- Where should microcard metrics live for customers on Dedicated vs Hosted? We should hide aggregated cost for Dedicated to avoid leaking infra details (privacy/contract).
- CON-912: acceptable estimator error threshold? propose <15% median error.

Acceptance and QA checklist (per ticket):
- Unit + integration test coverage for components.
- E2E happy path for keyboard users.
- Tracing: add span tags for feature flag and route id.
- Observability: add slow-query dashboard quicklink for microcard queries; rate-limit on estimator calls.

Sprint planning notes (facilitation):
- Slot a 30m grooming on Mon Aug 19 to finalize Run A scope and assign owners.
- Design to deliver final assets by Wed Aug 21. Devs to do spike for CON-871 backend compatibility by Thu Aug 22 (1 day).
- If Run A finishes early, pick CON-912 from Run B.

Cut rules (explicit):
- If an item pushes sprint dev load >13, drop lowest priority RUN A item where Impact <=3 and Effort >=3.
- Items with Risk >=2 require an explicit SRE sign-off; if sign-off unavailable, move to Run B.

Quick timeline (proposed):
- Aug 19: grooming and final scoring.
- Aug 21: design assets in Figma, basic tokens/colors.
- Aug 24: dev kickoff.
- Sep 7: close sprint, ship Run A.

Notes to self / follow-ups: 
- Maya: ping @Jon to get updated traffic percent distribution for estimator.
- Jon: open CON-980 spike for canary gating with SRE if we decide to require approvals.
- Priya: add acceptance example screenshots to CON-842.

Misc (working reminders):
- Keep the playlist small and predictable. Aim for 2 devs + 1 designer focused on Run A.
- Avoid adding "nice UX polish" items unless they are S-sized.
- Save larger experiments (A/B style large UI changes) for a separate design sprint.

-- end --
